title: Construction 8: Line segment of given length on a given ray
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: ray from A with arc cutting off B at 5 cm, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a ray starting at $A$. Construct the point $B$ on the ray so that $|AB| = 5$ cm.

steps.say: Place the compass point on $0$ on the ruler. Open the pencil to $5$ cm.

rows.aside: Do not change this setting until you have drawn the arc.

steps.say: Move the compass point to $A$. Swing the pencil so the arc crosses the ray.

rows.aside: Leave the arc on the page. It is the construction line.

issues: Label B sits above the ray at about x=690, but the arc crosses the ray further right at about x=730, so B is not at the crossing.
No dot or mark at the crossing point B.
The lower 5 cm ruler line ends at x=690, not at the arc, so the 5 cm span does not agree with the arc crossing.

title: Construction 2: Perpendicular bisector of a segment (compass and straight edge only)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: segment AB 8 cm with the arcs and the perpendicular bisector, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a segment $[AB]$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm. Using only a compass and straight edge, construct the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

steps.say: Open the compass to more than half of $|AB|$, about $5$ cm. Put the point on $A$ and draw an arc above and below the segment.

rows.aside: Do not change the setting until both arcs are drawn.

steps.say: Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw an arc above and below the segment, crossing the first two arcs.

rows.aside: The arcs cross at two points, one above $[AB]$ and one below.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line through the two crossing points. Mark where it cuts $[AB]$ and call that point $M$.

rows.aside: Leave every arc on the page. They are your construction lines and the marks are tied to them.
$|AM| = |MB| = 4$ cm and the line meets $[AB]$ at $90^\circ$.

issues: The arcs are drawn as a narrow dashed lens only about 10px wide, far smaller than arcs of radius about 5 cm on an 8 cm segment, so the arcs do not look like they come from A and B.
The label M sits on top of the perpendicular line and the segment, overlapping both.
The segment ends are not marked as points and there is no right-angle mark, so the figure shows little of what the steps describe.

title: Construction 3: Line perpendicular to a line l through a point not on l
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: line l, external point P, arcs and the perpendicular through P, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ above it. Construct the line through $P$ perpendicular to $l$.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. Open it wider than the distance from $P$ to $l$. Draw an arc that cuts $l$ in two places. Call them $A$ and $B$.

rows.aside: Now $|PA| = |PB|$, because both are the radius of the same arc.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc below $l$. Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw a second arc that crosses the first. Call the crossing $Q$.

rows.aside: Any setting works, as long as the two arcs cross.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line from $P$ to $Q$.

rows.aside: Leave every arc on the page. They are the construction lines.

issues: The label Q sits directly on the dashed arcs and the vertical line, so it is hard to read.
The arcs are mostly short stubs, so the arc crossing at Q is faint.

title: Construction 14: Right-angled triangle given one side and an acute angle
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: right triangle with AB 5 cm and angle A 50°, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct a right-angled triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 5$ cm, a right angle at $B$, and $\angle A = 50^\circ$.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a line segment $AB$ that is $5$ cm long.
Put the centre of the protractor on $A$ with its base along $AB$. Mark $50^\circ$, then draw a long line from $A$ through the mark.

rows.aside: Read from the zero that lies on $AB$.

steps.say: At $B$, construct the perpendicular to $AB$ with compass arcs. Draw a long line upward from $B$.

rows.aside: You can use a set square here instead, but arcs show the method.

steps.say: The two long lines cross. Call the crossing $C$.

issues: The label C is struck through by the vertical line and the long line from A at the top, so it is hard to read.
